substeps.caption: An example run on the alloy line: a build plate from the Aconity MIDI to the wire EDM, which cuts the tensile bars off it, then one bar to the Instron. The UR10e rides its MiR250 along the fronts.

The print is done: four ASTM E8 subsize tensile bars, 100 mm long and 6 mm thick, printed flat in AlSi10Mg on a 170 mm plate (DAL PR #169's build at Utah), and a handling lug for the gripper. They are still buried in the powder. The chamber is drawn see-through.

The print is done: four ASTM E8 subsize tensile bars, 100 mm long and 6 mm thick, printed flat in AlSi10Mg on a 170 mm plate (DAL PR #169's build at Utah), and a handling lug for the gripper. They are still buried in the powder. The chamber is drawn see-through.

The chamber door opens. Depowdering is a person's job: the MIDI has no automatic depowdering, so someone vacuums and brushes the loose powder off while the platform rises, and Aconity's separate sieve recovers it. The arm can't do this step.

The MiR250 rolls up. The platform's clamp lets go (a zero-point clamp: Aconity's platform takes a screwed plate, so this is an assumption). The chamber is 280 mm tall inside, too low for the gripper pointing down, so it takes the lug pointing 30° down and lifts the plate out.

To the Instron. The bar's 6 × 6 mm section at 412 MPa is a 14.8 kN pull: the 68SC-2 stops at 2 kN, so it goes to the 68FM-100 (100 kN). The crosshead rises out of the arm's way.

The crosshead comes down until the upper grip takes the bar's other end, 40 mm of it free between the jaws, and the upper grip closes.

The test: the crosshead pulls at a constant rate and the load cell reads the force. The curve is not a measurement: it runs through AddUp's published as-built values (AddUp AlSi10Mg data sheet, as built, XY, ASTM E8). The bar breaks at about 412 MPa, 5 % strain, with little necking.
Broken. The crosshead backs off 20 mm to show the break; the halves go on to the SEM for fractography.
Done: printed, cut and tested, every arm move a real one. Two steps still need a person or a new station: depowdering the build, and rinsing and drying the wet bars.
